title: Redistribution Layer Routing with Dynamic Via Insertion Under Irregular Via Structures
problem: Existing RDL routers perform via planning before routing, which limits the solution space and reduces layout flexibility when vias can be placed at arbitrary locations under irregular via structures. This pre-planned via approach restricts path-finding options during routing.
motivation: Improving routing quality and wirelength in redistribution layers is critical for advanced chip packaging systems that rely on vias for multi-layer signal transmission.
method: The method builds a routing graph supporting 90- and 135-degree connections, then searches for optimal paths while inserting vertical connectors (called vias) between layers on-the-fly instead of pre-planning their locations. This keeps vias flexible during the search—allowing the algorithm to place them wherever needed as it explores different routes—which opens up more possibilities than if via positions were locked in before routing started.
key_novelty: Placing vertical connectors between layers (vias) during the routing search itself, rather than pre-planning them before routing begins.
contributions: Novel routing graph model enabling dynamic via insertion for 90- and 135-degree routing
Over 10% better wirelength compared to state-of-the-art RDL routers
29X speedup over existing RDL routers with improved layout flexibility
55X speedup compared to any-angle routers with competitive wirelength

metrics.speedup: 29X vs state-of-the-art RDL routers, 55X vs any-angle router
metrics.other: 10% better wirelength, 0.4% better wirelength vs any-angle router
